title: CLAUDE.md
text: socialchange R package decomposing social change intraindividual change vs. population turnover. separates aggregate-level change time : - Intraindividual/within-unit change (people changing attitudes) - Population turnover (cohort replacement, mortality, migration, coming--age) - Event-driven change (countries joining/leaving EU) Intellectual positioning: (1) critique APC methods — suffer identification problem (age = period − cohort) need untestable assumptions; package offers directly interpretable decomposition alternatives. (2) improvement Firebaugh’s algebraic/linear CR-IC decomposition (mishandles entering/exiting cohorts, non-linearities, leaves residuals) via model-based counterfactuals (cr_ic()) simulation-based individual-level decomposition (sim_social_change(), decompose_aggregated()) tracks demographic events directly.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Three main decomposition approaches, using data.table, formula interfaces (Outcome ~ Unit + Time), S3 classes custom print()/plot(): Event-based (R/decompose_events.R) — decompose_events(): units enter/exit discrete times. Two datasets (events + outcomes). Separates “change” (within-unit) “replacement” (turnover) counterfactuals. → class decompose_events Aggregated (R/decompose_aggregated.R) — decompose_aggregated(): data aggregated age + covariates. Microsimulation randomly orders demographic events. Needs stacked panel data (age, period, cell counts) fitted model (lm/glm/gam) predicting outcome age/period/cells. Decomposes intraindividual change, coming--age, mortality, migration. Optional population arg supplies true cell × period count frame (overrides survey counts). Optional mortality arg (annual death probabilities period × age, optionally × cells) switches survivor-cell attribution sign attribution residual migration; result records strategy. R > 0 adds bootstrap SEs (combined ordering + model uncertainty). → class social_change_decomp. print plot methods live R/decompose_aggregated_output.R. Simulation (R/simulate.R) — sim_social_change(): forward simulation. User supplies functions outcome (fun_y), mortality, coming--age, migration, state transitions. Returns event--event records. → class social_change_sim Additional methods: - CR-IC (R/cr_ic.R) — classical cohort-replacement vs. intraindividual change (algebraic, linear, model-based). → class cr_ic_decomposition - APC (R/apc.R) — APC models via orthogonal polynomial contrasts; includes plot_gam_surface(). → class apc_model Functions rename input columns standardized names internally. decompose_aggregated() requires numeric period; cr_ic() validates periods/cohorts parse integers errors otherwise.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Events derived cell-count differences (“never residual”). New cohorts always get coming_of_age = pmax(0, n2 - n1). Survivor cells depend strategy stored strategy: sign attribution (default) mortality = pmax(0, n1 - n2), inmigration = pmax(0, n2 - n1), outmigration = 0; residual migration (mortality arg supplied) deaths = round(n1 × q̃) q̃ death probability compounded gap years (open group: per-constituent paths summed), migration signed residual n2 − (n1 − deaths). Consequences: Migration net per cell residual either strategy. Sign attribution: -migration never identified (survivor loss death exit, folded mortality; outmigration always 0), offsetting flows masked. Residual migration: -migration appears cell can carry deaths -migration, residual bundles genuine migration count-vs-rates inconsistency. raw survey cells either residual mostly sampling noise — mortality population, deaths round ~0 small cells nearly survivor change lands residual; meaningful true population frame. Migration among coming--age cohorts modeled. Open top age (“T+”). Survey waves share open outcome maximum T. population frame can extend T: true constituent ages drive mortality, predictions output clamped T. align_periods() pools period-1 constituents T−gap population terminal age one cell T, matched period-2 ages T+ (tick-0 y = constituents’ n-weighted prediction mean, kept per-replicate via "open_constituents"). population mortality frames must share one terminal open age; uncertainty within final open group remains. Hard eligibility cutoffs unsupported must labeled open groups. Transitions misattributed. Within-cell transitions (e.g. smokers → non-smokers) separately identified get absorbed intraindividual change; pmax(0, …) guard masks offsetting flows (cell net transition inflow shows 0 mortality even deaths occurred). Use data without significant transitions. sim_social_change() tracks transitions properly can’t recover aggregated data. Survey weights approximation. individual-level weight, weights normalized within period sum .N, n = round(sum(normalized_weight)). Adjusts relative structure correctly keeps event counts tractable, doesn’t recover absolute population sizes; rounding adds small errors. Prefer supplying true population counts available. Limitations bootstrap: Survey design ignored (reweights rows PSUs); population/mortality inputs held fixed across replicates (demographic uncertainty); refit reads original data name (getCall()$data), breaks scope; refitting transiently holds R refits (predictor keeps coefficients); replicates reuse one design matrix, model whose prediction isn’t fixed linkinv(Xβ) (weight-dependent basis) errors rather falling back per-replicate prediction.

GAM fun_y (s(age)+s(period)) ~75% wall time user’s model prediction, simulation logic: GAM call ~1.43 s (~1.08 s predict.gam/PredictMat), lm call ~0.35 s; simulation machinery ~0.35 s. simulate_schedule() evaluates fun_y n_cells × (n_ev+1) stacked frame, cost scales n_cells × n_ev × cost(fun_y) — bootstrap multiplies R. Bootstrap breakdown (cells="sex", R=100, GAM s(age)+s(period), model pre-fit, ~19.5 s total, Rprof): ~11.5 s 19.5 s mgcv’s compiled code (refit + predict); C++ side touch . Floor every optimization : ~10–11 s, ~90% mgcv. Moving past means cutting mgcv cost (lower R, fix sp, bam/discretization), R-vs-C++. Remaining leverage, highest first: - C++ port replay_schedule (~5 s, one big win side). O(n_ev × n_cells × K) replay loop (K = max(R, 1) columns, one per (ordering, draw) replicate); RNG, deterministic — natural Rcpp unit. Runs 2×(n_periods−1) times K=R. Per-column vectorized replay already spent; ~5.8 s → <1 s C++. - Pure-R: share stack lpmatrix point draws (~2 s). transition hits PredictMat twice stack — predict_y(model, stack) (point) make_X(stack) inside replicate_predict (draws). title: Cohort replacement vs. intracohort change decomposition — cr_ic
text: - **AD** (algebraic decomposition): Decomposes spanning cohorts IC   CR exactly. Entering exiting cohorts split assigned   entirely CR, Firebaugh notes "problematic". - **LD** (linear decomposition): Fits linear model `y ~ period + cohort`   uses coefficients attribute change. Handles entering/exiting   cohorts capture non-linearities produces residual. - **AD+**: Extends AD imputing missing outcome values entering/exiting   cohorts model supplied via `model`, applies algebraic   decomposition. Produces residual; quality depends model fit. - **Model**: Like AD+ replaces ** cohort-specific values (just   missing ones) model predictions. Acts form regularization,   can help small cohorts noisy estimates. AD LD always computed. AD+ Model require `model` argument.
